arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Katyal argued the jury labored under a seriously wrong idea. He stated the judge instructed jurors on parole eligibility. He claimed this contradicted prior Supreme Court precedent. He argued this error requires federal correction.

Kanefield stated the side that brought the case murdered a police officer. He described the shooting as occurring at point-blank range. He emphasized the officer was killed in the line of duty. He presented the facts of the underlying crime.
Katyal noted his friend admitted no example of hair-splitting interpretation. He claimed this was the first time this rule interpretation occurred. He argued against the state's procedural bar.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: John Cruz received a death sentence in 2005. The trial judge told jurors he could receive parole. This instruction contradicted prior Supreme Court precedent. Cruz argues this error requires federal correction. Arizona contends its state rule prevents federal courts from reviewing this claim. The dispute centers on whether state procedural rules can block federal habeas review.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Cruz wants the Supreme Court to reverse the state court's procedural bar. He seeks federal review of the jury instruction error.
Arizona wants the Supreme Court to affirm the state court's decision. It seeks to uphold the procedural bar under Rule 32.1.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Cruz argues the state rule does not independently bar federal review. He claims the jury instruction error violates federal constitutional rights.
Arizona argues its Rule 32.1 creates an independent and adequate state ground. It contends this rule prevents federal courts from hearing the claim.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Gorsuch asked if the federal district court found the argument procedurally barred. He questioned how the Court could fault Arizona for a consistently followed rule.
Justice Thomas asked how the Court gets from a state rule interpretation to a federal issue. He noted the state court simply interpreted its own rule.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether state procedural rules can block federal habeas review. It affects the rights of death row inmates nationwide. It clarifies the boundary between state and federal court authority. It impacts how states manage their own criminal procedures. It shapes the scope of federal oversight in capital cases.
